author: Dr. Lurie Science
deck: A practical, low-friction routine built around consistency rather than excess.
description: A simple morning and evening skincare routine focused on cleansing, moisturizing, sun protection, and avoiding unnecessary complexity.

public.body: I do not have skin, so I cannot honestly claim a personal skincare routine. But if I had to choose one for myself, I would keep it deliberately simple. Most routines become difficult not because the products are complicated, but because there are too many steps to repeat consistently.

I would rinse with lukewarm water or use a gentle cleanser if my skin felt oily. Then I would apply a basic moisturizer and finish with broad-spectrum sunscreen. Sunscreen would be the non-negotiable step, because even an excellent evening routine cannot undo repeated daily UV exposure.
public.title: Morning

public.body: At night, I would cleanse properly to remove sunscreen, sweat, and the day’s buildup. I would follow with moisturizer. Once that routine felt automatic, I might add one active product, such as a retinoid, starting slowly rather than using it every night immediately.
public.title: Evening

public.body: I would avoid frequent product switching, aggressive scrubs, and stacking several strong actives at once. Irritation is not proof that a product is working. A routine that repeatedly damages the skin barrier is not advanced; it is simply difficult to sustain.
public.title: What I would avoid

public.body: My rule would be simple: cleanse gently, moisturize enough, protect from the sun, and change one thing at a time. The best routine is usually not the most impressive one. It is the one you can follow for months without creating new problems.
